strategic_context: Across Canada and within the federal public service, there is a clear expectation that institutions deliver tangible results with focus, discipline, and speed.
Leaders are being called upon to strengthen productivity, make explicit choices about priorities, and demonstrate value in practical terms.
At the same time, fiscal realities require thoughtful stewardship and sharper alignment of resources to outcomes.

For Statistics Canada, this context demands an agenda that is both ambitious and deliberate—one that reinforces operational excellence, accelerates modernization, strengthens our digital and methodological foundations, and equips our people to execute with clarity and confidence.
The Economic Statistics Field plays a critical role in this agenda.

As the producer of core macroeconomic indicators—including gross domestic product, inflation, trade, and sectoral statistics—your field provides essential inputs to fiscal and monetary policy, federal transfers, and economic decision-making at all levels.
These outputs are not only foundational to Canada’s economic governance, but also to public confidence in the country’s economic performance and resilience.

Your work positions Statistics Canada as a trusted and responsive data partner across government, ensuring that decision-makers have access to timely, relevant, and high-quality data, while maintaining independence and confidentiality.

Delivering on these priorities will require explicit alignment of resources—including funding, workforce, and executive attention—with enterprise priorities, and disciplined trade-offs where activities do not support scaled implementation.
At the same time, the integrity, coherence, and credibility of Canada’s core economic statistics must be sustained.

In a context of fiscal constraint, evolving data sources, and increasing demand for timely insight, this means continuing to deliver mission-critical programs that directly inform monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic stability.
Strengthening how the value and impact of these statistics are communicated—linking outputs to real-world outcomes and public understanding—will be essential to reinforcing trust and relevance.
This includes advancing key initiatives such as the implementation of the System of National Accounts 2025 and the development of the TechStats program.
This also depends on sustaining a respectful, inclusive, and accountable workplace during a period of sustained change.
Workforce adjustment, skills transition, and modernization efforts require steady leadership grounded in fairness and clarity.

Advancing reconciliation in practical ways, strengthening inclusive practices, and reinforcing leadership accountability for supporting and developing people will be key to maintaining engagement and trust.
I encourage you to insist on clarity, maintain focus on outcomes, and model disciplined execution.
Where trade-offs are required, make them explicit.
Where timelines are set, manage actively to them.
Perfection is not the objective—timely, high-quality delivery is.

Field 5 2026 mandate letter
April 24, 2026
Jennifer Withington
            Assistant Chief Statistician
            Economic Statistics Field
            Statistics Canada
            100 Tunney’s Pasture
            Ottawa, Ontario, K1A 0T6
            R.H. Coats Building
Dear Jennifer,
Thank you for your continued leadership as Assistant Chief Statistician for the Economic Statistics Field. Your work is central to ensuring that Statistics Canada delivers the trusted economic indicators that underpin decision-making across governments, markets, and institutions.
Across Canada and within the federal public service, there is a clear expectation that institutions deliver tangible results with focus, discipline, and speed. Leaders are being called upon to strengthen productivity, make explicit choices about priorities, and demonstrate value in practical terms. At the same time, fiscal realities require thoughtful stewardship and sharper alignment of resources to outcomes. For Statistics Canada, this context demands an agenda that is both ambitious and deliberate—one that reinforces operational excellence, accelerates modernization, strengthens our digital and methodological foundations, and equips our people to execute with clarity and confidence.
The Economic Statistics Field plays a critical role in this agenda. As the producer of core macroeconomic indicators—including gross domestic product, inflation, trade, and sectoral statistics—your field provides essential inputs to fiscal and monetary policy, federal transfers, and economic decision-making at all levels. These outputs are not only foundational to Canada’s economic governance, but also to public confidence in the country’s economic performance and resilience. Your work positions Statistics Canada as a trusted and responsive data partner across government, ensuring that decision-makers have access to timely, relevant, and high-quality data, while maintaining independence and confidentiality.
In keeping with your role as described above, the following corporate priorities will guide your field’s work. I ask that you articulate and communicate how they are being advanced within your field:
- Delivering the 2026 Census of Population and Census of Agriculture
 Ensure the successful delivery of the 2026 Census of Population and Census of Agriculture, including secure collection, processing and dissemination, systems stability, operational resilience, and public and stakeholder confidence—while managing heightened fiscal, workforce, and reputational risk.
- Advancing next-generation statistical production
 Accelerate enterprise adoption of corporate platforms, integrated data pipelines, modern data management practices, administrative and alternative data, automation, and advanced methods—including artificial intelligence where it demonstrably adds value. Move beyond pilots to sustained, enterprise-scale implementation. Continue delivering the agency’s core statistical programs that support legislation and policy direction, with measurable reductions in manual effort, respondent burden, and cycle time.
- Modernizing and securing the agency’s digital foundations
 Strengthen cyber security, privacy, and secure access while modernizing platforms, authorizations, and tooling to support faster delivery and safer innovation.
- Strengthening workforce sustainability and leadership capacity
 Support employees and leaders through workforce adjustment, skills transition (data, methods, digital), and cultural change—while sustaining engagement, clarity, and trust.
- Clarifying enterprise governance and reinforcing decision discipline
 Strengthen prioritization, accountability, and cross-field decision-making so scarce resources are focused on the highest-value outcomes and trade-offs are transparent.
- Increasing enterprise agility and execution discipline
 Commit to fixed timelines and clear delivery milestones and manage actively to those deadlines. Accelerate decision-making and implementation by clarifying authorities, removing barriers, and aligning resources to time-critical outcomes. Foster a culture of action over prolonged deliberation—while maintaining sound stewardship and risk management.
Delivering on these priorities will require explicit alignment of resources—including funding, workforce, and executive attention—with enterprise priorities, and disciplined trade-offs where activities do not support scaled implementation.
At the same time, the integrity, coherence, and credibility of Canada’s core economic statistics must be sustained. In a context of fiscal constraint, evolving data sources, and increasing demand for timely insight, this means continuing to deliver mission-critical programs that directly inform monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic stability. Strengthening how the value and impact of these statistics are communicated—linking outputs to real-world outcomes and public understanding—will be essential to reinforcing trust and relevance. This includes advancing key initiatives such as the implementation of the System of National Accounts 2025 and the development of the TechStats program.
This also depends on sustaining a respectful, inclusive, and accountable workplace during a period of sustained change. Workforce adjustment, skills transition, and modernization efforts require steady leadership grounded in fairness and clarity. Advancing reconciliation in practical ways, strengthening inclusive practices, and reinforcing leadership accountability for supporting and developing people will be key to maintaining engagement and trust.
I encourage you to insist on clarity, maintain focus on outcomes, and model disciplined execution. Where trade-offs are required, make them explicit. Where timelines are set, manage actively to them. Perfection is not the objective—timely, high-quality delivery is.
I look forward to continuing our work together to ensure that the Economic Statistics Field continues to deliver the high-quality, trusted data that supports Canada’s economic strength, resilience, and informed decision-making.
Sincerely,
André Loranger
            Chief Statistician of Canada

strategic_context: The Economic Statistics Field plays a central role in Canada’s economic governance.
Our programs produce the core macroeconomic statistics that underpin monetary and fiscal policy, federal transfers, legislative requirements, and public understanding of economic conditions.

In a context of fiscal restraint, heightened delivery expectations, shifting trade and geopolitical conditions, and accelerating technological change, our responsibility remains clear: to sustain trusted, high‑quality core outputs while continuing to modernize how we produce them.
This mandate sets out priorities that will guide our work over the coming year.
These priorities are intended to support focus and disciplined execution, with clear and transparent decision-making.
They require us to make explicit choices, so effort and resources are aligned to the highest value outcomes.

priorities.title: Integrating artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows
priorities.original_description: We will continue to integrate artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows and to streamline processes across the Generic Statistical Business Process Model. This work is intended to improve efficiency, reduce manual effort, and better support the ongoing production of core statistical programs. Emphasis will be placed on approaches that can be embedded directly into production workflows, reduce duplication, and clarify handoffs across programs. Automation and advanced methods, including artificial intelligence where it demonstrably adds value, will be applied to support reliable and repeatable production rather than experimentation alone. This work will continue to align with enterprise platforms and shared solutions and will be supported by appropriate governance, documentation, and monitoring. The objective is to strengthen the sustainability and consistency of production while maintaining quality, transparency, and public trust.

priorities.title: Strengthening workforce sustainability and leadership capacity
priorities.original_description: Our people are central to delivering on this mandate. We will continue to strengthen workforce sustainability by supporting employees and equipping managers to lead teams effectively through transitions while maintaining safe, respectful, and supportive work environments. In 2026/2027, this includes supporting employees and leaders through workforce adjustment pressures, skills transition in data, methods, and digital tools, and cultural change associated with modernization and evolving ways of working. The transition to new tools, methods, and data sources will require sustained attention to training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of work alongside production demands. We will continue to strengthen leadership capacity among managers and supervisors, with emphasis on clarity of roles, responsibilities, and priorities in a constrained and changing environment. Clear communication, consistent performance management, and attention to employee well‑being will be essential to sustaining engagement, clarity, and trust. Managers are expected to work within prescribed timelines and to exercise disciplined decision‑making, fostering a culture of action over prolonged deliberation. Issues should be resolved at the appropriate level, with leaders taking ownership of decisions within their accountabilities.

priorities.title: Advancing the transition to open‑source environments
priorities.original_description: The transition to open-source environments will continue as an important component of transformation across the field. In 2026/2027, this transition will focus on sustaining previous progress with greater emphasis on validation, upskilling and governance. Work will continue to prioritize reusable solutions and shared components, with development aligned to enterprise architecture to support interoperability, scalable solutions and long-term sustainability. Teams will be supported as they continue to adopt open‑source tools while meeting ongoing production responsibilities, including through training and collaborative development practices. This work will be guided by the need to maintain secure and stable production environments and the capacity required to support solutions over time. Decisions will reflect accountability for secure, stable, and reliable delivery.

priorities.title: Sustaining high-quality core economic statistics
priorities.original_description: At the centre of this mandate is our responsibility to deliver high‑quality, trusted core economic statistics in a timely manner. This responsibility is non‑negotiable and remains the primary consideration in setting priorities and allocating resources. This includes responsible data stewardship and ongoing efforts to improve how diverse forms of economic activity are reflected in official statistics. In 2026/2027, this includes the successful delivery of the 2026 Census of Agriculture. This major operation requires secure collection, processing, and dissemination; systems stability and operational resilience; and sustained public and stakeholder confidence. Its delivery will require careful management of fiscal, workforce and operational resources, as well as close coordination across the agency. We will continue to streamline operations and identify opportunities to strengthen quality, coherence, and consistency in cross-field collaboration. We will also advance implementation of the 2025 System of National Accounts to ensure comprehensive data and international relevance. The delivery of core outputs that support legislation, monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic decision‑making will remain the field’s foremost priority. Programs will continue to adapt to emerging analytical and policy needs. This includes strengthening measurement of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies through TechStat; providing timely and relevant insights on Canada–U.S. economic relations, including trade, tourism, investment, and ownership; and supporting key policy domains such as defense, energy, critical minerals, environmental and ecosystem accounting, and northern economic development. Increased use of administrative and alternative data sources will continue to support these efforts while managing respondent burden. Where capacity constraints require trade-offs, they will be made explicitly and transparently, with resources focused on protecting mission critical programs and maintaining public trust in Canada’s economic statistics.

source_title: Field 5 2026 mandate letter from Jennifer Withington
source_content:
Field 5 2026 mandate letter from Jennifer Withington
May 22, 2026
All staff
            Economic Statistics Field
            Statistics Canada
Colleagues,
I want to begin by thanking you for your continued professionalism, commitment, and resilience during this period of sustained change across the agency. Following the mandate letter I received from the Chief Statistician, I am writing to outline how the Economic Statistics Field will advance the agency’s priorities in 2026/2027 and what this will mean in practical terms for our work.
The Economic Statistics Field plays a central role in Canada’s economic governance. Our programs produce the core macroeconomic statistics that underpin monetary and fiscal policy, federal transfers, legislative requirements, and public understanding of economic conditions. In a context of fiscal restraint, heightened delivery expectations, shifting trade and geopolitical conditions, and accelerating technological change, our responsibility remains clear: to sustain trusted, high‑quality core outputs while continuing to modernize how we produce them.
This mandate sets out priorities that will guide our work over the coming year. These priorities are intended to support focus and disciplined execution, with clear and transparent decision-making. They require us to make explicit choices, so effort and resources are aligned to the highest value outcomes.
Integrating artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows
We will continue to integrate artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows and to streamline processes across the Generic Statistical Business Process Model. This work is intended to improve efficiency, reduce manual effort, and better support the ongoing production of core statistical programs.
Emphasis will be placed on approaches that can be embedded directly into production workflows, reduce duplication, and clarify handoffs across programs. Automation and advanced methods, including artificial intelligence where it demonstrably adds value, will be applied to support reliable and repeatable production rather than experimentation alone.
This work will continue to align with enterprise platforms and shared solutions and will be supported by appropriate governance, documentation, and monitoring. The objective is to strengthen the sustainability and consistency of production while maintaining quality, transparency, and public trust.
Strengthening workforce sustainability and leadership capacity
Our people are central to delivering on this mandate. We will continue to strengthen workforce sustainability by supporting employees and equipping managers to lead teams effectively through transitions while maintaining safe, respectful, and supportive work environments.
In 2026/2027, this includes supporting employees and leaders through workforce adjustment pressures, skills transition in data, methods, and digital tools, and cultural change associated with modernization and evolving ways of working. The transition to new tools, methods, and data sources will require sustained attention to training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of work alongside production demands.
We will continue to strengthen leadership capacity among managers and supervisors, with emphasis on clarity of roles, responsibilities, and priorities in a constrained and changing environment. Clear communication, consistent performance management, and attention to employee well‑being will be essential to sustaining engagement, clarity, and trust. Managers are expected to work within prescribed timelines and to exercise disciplined decision‑making, fostering a culture of action over prolonged deliberation. Issues should be resolved at the appropriate level, with leaders taking ownership of decisions within their accountabilities.
Advancing the transition to open‑source environments
The transition to open-source environments will continue as an important component of transformation across the field. In 2026/2027, this transition will focus on sustaining previous progress with greater emphasis on validation, upskilling and governance.
Work will continue to prioritize reusable solutions and shared components, with development aligned to enterprise architecture to support interoperability, scalable solutions and long-term sustainability. Teams will be supported as they continue to adopt open‑source tools while meeting ongoing production responsibilities, including through training and collaborative development practices.
This work will be guided by the need to maintain secure and stable production environments and the capacity required to support solutions over time. Decisions will reflect accountability for secure, stable, and reliable delivery.
Sustaining high-quality core economic statistics
At the centre of this mandate is our responsibility to deliver high‑quality, trusted core economic statistics in a timely manner. This responsibility is non‑negotiable and remains the primary consideration in setting priorities and allocating resources. This includes responsible data stewardship and ongoing efforts to improve how diverse forms of economic activity are reflected in official statistics.
In 2026/2027, this includes the successful delivery of the 2026 Census of Agriculture. This major operation requires secure collection, processing, and dissemination; systems stability and operational resilience; and sustained public and stakeholder confidence. Its delivery will require careful management of fiscal, workforce and operational resources, as well as close coordination across the agency.
We will continue to streamline operations and identify opportunities to strengthen quality, coherence, and consistency in cross-field collaboration. We will also advance implementation of the 2025 System of National Accounts to ensure comprehensive data and international relevance. The delivery of core outputs that support legislation, monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic decision‑making will remain the field’s foremost priority.
Programs will continue to adapt to emerging analytical and policy needs. This includes strengthening measurement of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies through TechStat; providing timely and relevant insights on Canada–U.S. economic relations, including trade, tourism, investment, and ownership; and supporting key policy domains such as defense, energy, critical minerals, environmental and ecosystem accounting, and northern economic development. Increased use of administrative and alternative data sources will continue to support these efforts while managing respondent burden.
Where capacity constraints require trade-offs, they will be made explicitly and transparently, with resources focused on protecting mission critical programs and maintaining public trust in Canada’s economic statistics.
Moving forward
Delivering on this mandate will require focus, discipline, and collective effort. It will also require strong critical thinking to ensure clarity about what we will not do, where simplification is necessary, and how resources are aligned in support of successful outcomes.
Leaders at all levels are expected to manage actively to achieve timelines and delivery milestones, strengthen prioritization and accountability, and support timely decision‑making. This includes maintaining alignment with agreed priorities and ensuring decisions and actions support delivery. As we do so, we will maintain sound risk management and accountability for delivery while continuing to produce the high-quality statistics that Canadians rely on.
Thank you for the professionalism and dedication you bring to this work each day. Together, I am confident we will continue to deliver trusted, relevant statistics that inform decisions and support Canada’s economic well‑being.
Sincerely,
Jennifer Withington
            Assistant Chief Statistician
            Economic Statistics Field

priorities.title: Deliver social statistical programs aligned with government priorities
priorities.original_description:
Lead efforts to enhance housing statistics by producing high-quality information on housing supply, affordability, and outcomes. The field will improve the coverage, frequency, and timeliness of data on housing stock, residential construction and rental prices, and collaborate with Government of Canada partners to inform housing priorities.

The field will provide strategic leadership for the National Justice Statistics Initiative (NJSI), delivering authoritative information on crime, victimization and the administration of justice in Canada. In 2026/2027, you will advance the NJSI priority on Bail and Recontact Data Enhancement by standardizing definitions and data collection protocols and partnering with courts, corrections, law enforcement, and community organizations to improve data completeness and timeliness.

It will lead the delivery of the statistical indicators measuring progress under the Federal Provincial Territories Shared Health Priorities initiative, and oversee Statistics Canada’s contribution to the proposal for the new Health & Life Sciences Data, Research and Infrastructure Collaboratorium initiative. The field will also advance streamlining efforts within the Health Statistics Program to support the financial viability of the Canadian Health Measures Survey and continue implementing the Overdose Crisis Data Program to address critical data gaps.

The field will continue to deliver high-quality Quality-of-Life measures by addressing the remaining objectives identified in the 2024/2025 Biennial Review, launching the 2026/2027 Biennial Review and adopting recommendations from the program evaluation. As a field, we will also strengthen dissemination, analysis, and data discoverability through the Quality-of-Life Hub, including improvements to automation, data pipelines and interoperability. Across these areas, efforts will aim to improve timeliness, reduce production burden where possible, and enhance the accessibility and usefulness of outputs for decision-makers.

Field 8 2026 mandate letter from Josée Bégin
May 22, 2026
All staff
            Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field
            Statistics Canada
Dear colleagues of the Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field,
Thank you for your continued dedication to producing high‑quality social, health, and labour statistics. Your work helps decision‑makers and Canadians rely on solid evidence and better reflect the real experiences of people in Canada. It plays an important role in reinforcing Statistics Canada as a trusted and relevant source of statistics and insights in Canada’s social data landscape.
The operating environment for the coming year continues to demand focus, discipline, and clarity of execution. Fiscal constraints, evolving data sources, and increasing expectations for timely, disaggregated, and policy-relevant information require deliberate prioritization, explicit trade-offs, and strong program stewardship. In this context, we will continue to focus on timely decision-making, clear priorities, and managing our work against defined timelines, while making thoughtful trade-offs to concentrate efforts where they will have the greatest impact. Within this context, and based on the direction set out in my mandate letter from the Chief Statistician, the following priorities will guide the work of the Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field in 2026/2027.
1. Deliver the 2026 Census of Population
Ensure the successful delivery of the 2026 Census of Population, including the tracking and monitoring of data quality during collection and processing and finalization of quality measurement tools and certification of results. You will lead the development and implementation of a comprehensive analysis strategy and the delivery of final dissemination content, beginning with the release of key reference products and the dissemination of 2026 Census data and analysis. Your work will help ensure that Canadians have access to relevant, accurate and timely census data that reflect Canada’s changing society and support the development and delivery of social programs in alignment with government priorities. This work will be supported by ongoing monitoring of progress against timelines and a clear focus on delivery at each stage.
2. Deliver social statistical programs aligned with government priorities
Lead efforts to enhance housing statistics by producing high-quality information on housing supply, affordability, and outcomes. The field will improve the coverage, frequency, and timeliness of data on housing stock, residential construction and rental prices, and collaborate with Government of Canada partners to inform housing priorities.
The field will provide strategic leadership for the National Justice Statistics Initiative (NJSI), delivering authoritative information on crime, victimization and the administration of justice in Canada. In 2026/2027, you will advance the NJSI priority on Bail and Recontact Data Enhancement by standardizing definitions and data collection protocols and partnering with courts, corrections, law enforcement, and community organizations to improve data completeness and timeliness.
It will lead the delivery of the statistical indicators measuring progress under the Federal Provincial Territories Shared Health Priorities initiative, and oversee Statistics Canada’s contribution to the proposal for the new Health & Life Sciences Data, Research and Infrastructure Collaboratorium initiative. The field will also advance streamlining efforts within the Health Statistics Program to support the financial viability of the Canadian Health Measures Survey and continue implementing the Overdose Crisis Data Program to address critical data gaps.
The field will continue to deliver high-quality Quality-of-Life measures by addressing the remaining objectives identified in the 2024/2025 Biennial Review, launching the 2026/2027 Biennial Review and adopting recommendations from the program evaluation. As a field, we will also strengthen dissemination, analysis, and data discoverability through the Quality-of-Life Hub, including improvements to automation, data pipelines and interoperability. Across these areas, efforts will aim to improve timeliness, reduce production burden where possible, and enhance the accessibility and usefulness of outputs for decision-makers.
3. Advance transformation initiatives
The field will advance transformation initiatives to modernize statistical production and support efficient, high-quality delivery in line with the December 2028 deadline. This will be achieved through your work in the transition to open-source environments by coordinating field activities, providing technical support, and managing milestones and risks in collaboration with enterprise partners. The field will transition programs to modern corporate platforms to enable integrated, metadata-driven pipelines that support automation and enterprise best practices, while maintaining the rigour and reliability of monthly production. As part of this work, Field 8 will deliver on the modernization of the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours and the Labour Force Survey, simplifying and streamlining processing, improving data quality, reducing manual intervention, and strengthening program stewardship. Our field will advance the redesign of the General Social Statistics Program to meet the ever-increasing data needs. These efforts are expected to contribute to more efficient production processes, including reducing manual steps, supporting timelier outputs, and increasing opportunities for reuse through enterprise approaches.
Delivering on these priorities will require disciplined alignment of resources, active management of timelines, and clear accountability for outcomes. Managers and supervisors play a key role in setting direction, supporting timely decisions, and helping teams remain focused on priority deliverables. Where timelines are set, progress should be managed actively to support delivery, while continuing to foster a respectful and supportive work environment as we look to the future.
I thank you again for your continued leadership and dedication, and for approaching this year with focus and professionalism.
Sincerely,
Josée Bégin
            Assistant Chief Statistician
            Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field
